core_obligations: Gorenstein (proof lines 6095-6097): nodal curves have invertible omega_X.

Genus 0 (proof lines 6099-6104): deg(omega_X) < 0 contradicts the tail inequalities in the reducible case; the irreducible case is the plane conic with omega_X^tensor -1 very ample by lemma-genus-zero.

Genus 1 (proof lines 6106-6115): deg(omega_X|_C) >= 0 on every component by the tail inequalities, the componentwise sum is 0 by lemma-genus-gorenstein and the degree-in-components lemma, so all degrees vanish and omega_X is trivial by the no-sections duality lemma.

Genus >= 2 (proof lines 6117-6130): irreducible case is lemma-degree-more-than-2g; in the reducible case the tail inequalities give the global-generation hypotheses for every proper Y, and the only Y = X inequalities used in the proof of lemma-global-generation both hold for m >= 2 and g >= 2.
proof_roadmap: Fix invertibility of omega_X from nodality.
Dispatch genus 0 by the tail contradiction or the conic classification.
Dispatch genus 1 by componentwise degree bookkeeping and the duality lemma.
Dispatch genus >= 2 by the irreducible lemma and, in the reducible case, by checking the two Y = X inequalities directly.
difficulty_reason: The lemma describes curves without rational tails in each genus (statement lines 6080-6093). The proof (lines 6095-6130) is a complete three-case chain: Gorenstein input, the genus-0 dichotomy (tail contradiction versus conic classification), the genus-1 vanishing of componentwise degrees with the duality conclusion, and the genus->=2 case combining the irreducible lemma with an explicit re-analysis of the two Y = X inequalities in the global-generation proof, which the author states in full. Every step is present with no omissions. H2: systematic case analysis with correctly ordered reference hinges.
